title: Token mix sensitivity by customer segment (mid-cycle testbed)
content:
Purpose:
A compact mid-cycle working note to capture an exploratory sensitivity run that ties token mix shifts (startup/SMB/enterprise) to revenue, gross margin, and a micro headcount plan. This is a testbed model — not the canonical FY27 submission — intended to help product and sales prioritize small pricing and packaging experiments that materially change unit economics.

Executive summary (2 lines):
- Small shifts in token mix toward higher-context enterprise requests yield outsized margin improvements because enterprise calls skew toward embeddings+long-context generation which we can serve with higher cache hit rates and fewer early truncations.
- There is a narrow band of price increases (2–4%) that materially preserves volume for Enterprise while improving unit margins for SMB. For Startups, elasticity is higher; monitor churn signals.

Key assumptions: (explicit so experiments are reproducible)
- Customer segments: Startups (S), SMB (M), Enterprise (E). Current ARR mix: S 30%, M 45%, E 25%.
- Token mix (by percent of total tokens served): generation-short (<=512): 48%, generation-long (>512): 22%, embeddings: 20%, rerankings/other: 10%.
- Average price per 1k tokens (baseline): S $0.008, M $0.010, E $0.012 (weighted by route and committed discounts).
- Elasticity (volume change per +1% price): S -1.8%, M -0.9%, E -0.3%. (source: surface-level cohort tests Apr–Jun and sales feedback)
- Gross contribution margin per token before fixed infra and headcount: baseline compute+storage+network = $0.0047 / 1k tokens (weighted by model mix).
- Customer-level prefix caching improvement for E under proposed routing strategy = +12% effective token reduction on average for long-gen and embeddings.

Model layout (high-level):
- Inputs: current ARR by segment, baseline token usage per month, token mix split, price per 1k token per segment, elasticity matrix, cache improvement scenarios, marginal cost per token.
- Outputs: delta ARR (monthly), delta gross margin (monthly), incremental contribution dollars, suggested HC hires or hiring freezes triggered by net contribution thresholds.

Scenario runs (summary):
1) Baseline (no price change, cache improvements as-is)
   - Monthly tokens: 95B (baseline)
   - Monthly revenue: $1.02M
   - Gross margin: 51%
   - Hiring trigger: maintain hiring cadence (no change)

2) +3% uniform price increase across segments
   - Volume impact using elasticities: overall -2.0% tokens
   - Revenue delta: +1.0% (revenue increases despite small drop in volume)
   - Gross margin: +2.6 pp (points)
   - Net contribution change: +$10.8k / month
   - Hiring trigger: approve 1 frontend infra hire (if >$10k/month sustained), else hold

3) Targeted +4% on SMB, +1% on Enterprise, 0% on Startups + enterprise cache-improvement +12% effective token reduction on E long-gen
   - Net tokens change: -0.8% overall
   - Revenue delta: +2.1% (net uplift driven by SMB price)
   - Gross margin: +4.1 pp (improvement concentrated on E due to cache benefits)
   - Net contribution change: +$37.5k / month
   - Hiring trigger: greenlight 2 hires (1 infra ops, 1 account manager for enterprise expansion) with 6-month payback horizon

4) Defensive test: Startups price -5% promotional credit to spur volume (paired with SMB +2%)
   - Startups volume up +9% (elasticity applied), SMB down -1.8% net
   - Revenue delta: flat to -0.4% depending on startup conversion cadence
   - Gross margin: -1.9 pp (promotional pressure)
   - Hiring trigger: hiring freeze for product headcount; continue critical infra hires only

Micro headcount plan (quarterly phasing):
- Baseline hiring plan for next 6 months (starting Aug 2026):
  - Infra: +3 (Q3: +1, Q4: +2)
  - Product (SDK/console): +2 (Q4)
  - Sales/AM (enterprise coverage): +2 (staged Q4 if scenario 3 chosen)
  - Finance/ops: +1 (headcount to support committed capacity billing)
- Cost per hire (fully loaded, monthly): Infra $18k, Product $15k, Sales/AM $13k, Finance $12k
- Break-even thresholds (contribution required to justify hire within 6 months): Infra $108k, Product $90k, Sales/AM $78k, Finance $72k

Sensitivity table (key cells extracted):
- If SMB price +3% and elasticity -0.9% -> SMB revenue +2.1% ; company revenue +1.6% ; gross margin +2.8 pp
- If Enterprise cache improvement +12% -> token demand for E down 7% but contribution up 9% (due to lower marginal cost)
- If Startups price +2% -> tokens -3.6% ; revenue -1.7% ; monitor churn cohorts 0–60 days

Operational recommendations (short list):
- Run a 6-week A/B test for scenario 3 with a 30% sample of SMB accounts and 50% sample of new enterprise traffic to validate elasticities. Add measurement hooks for churn, NPS, and feature usage.
- Implement routing rule POC: pin long-context enterprise sessions to cache-optimized cluster for the bundle; add metrics for cache-hit ratio by customer tag.
- Finance to maintain a weekly variance dashboard during the test window: tokens/day, revenue/day, cache-hit ratio, new churn signals.
- Hold non-critical product hires until the test completes unless test signals exceed thresholds (revenue +3% sustained).

Open questions / risks: (working list)
- Accuracy of elasticity estimates for SMB: current cohorts are small (n<120) and heavily influenced by seasonal renewals. Consider Bayesian shrinkage in final model.
- Sales acceptance risk of targeted price increases — requires uplift compensation plan in contracts and careful communication.
- Operational complexity of routing change: likely requires one infra sprint and a short security review for tenant isolation.

Next steps (owner / ETA):
- Finance to instrument the test model in the forecasting workbook (owner: Jordan P) — ETA 2026-07-26
- Product to prototype routing POC for enterprise long-gen caching (owner: Priya S) — ETA 2026-08-10
- Sales to identify 80 SMB accounts for pilot and 6 enterprise customers open to reduced-price pilot in exchange for cache routing (owner: Carlos M) — ETA 2026-07-30

Appendix: brief data appendix and quick numbers
- Baseline monthly tokens by segment (est): S 28.5B, M 42.75B, E 23.75B
- Baseline revenue mix (monthly): S $228k, M $457k, E $335k
- Baseline marginal cost (compute/storage/network): S $134k, M $226k, E $105k

Notes to reviewer: this doc intentionally keeps the balancing logic compact. If this testbed looks promising, I will push a full workbook with scenario tabs (price-bands, elasticity sensitivity grid, hiring-payback tab) into the forecasting repo and link.

-- Jordan
